original_question: Suppose an r-vector is an arithmetic progression with difference Delta. Beyond the Cartesian exponentials of the 2-element and 3-element chains, do there exist any finite distributive differential posets with such r-vectors when Delta < 0, and can all Delta < 0 cases be classified completely?
target_in_paper: Section 2 (Problems of 2025), Problem 44, with notation L(r) inherited from Problem 42.
correct_elements: Your draft already captures the exact open problem in Problem 44: it keeps the arithmetic-progression hypothesis on the r-vector, focuses on the negative-difference regime Δ < 0, excludes the Cartesian powers of the 2-element and 3-element chains, and asks for a complete classification of the remaining Δ < 0 cases.
missing_details: The paper's notation L(r) is inherited from Problem 42: for a vector r, L(r) denotes an r-differential distributive lattice, if one exists; this is not stated in the draft.

The draft does not say that the r-vector is the vector of rank-dependent differential parameters used in the sequentially differential generalization referenced in [Stan1990, sec. 2]; the notebook does not restate this definition locally.

The paper frames the question inside the arithmetic-progression subclass of those r-vectors, with common difference Δ, and records the background facts Δ ≤ 0, that Δ = 0 gives the ordinary differential-poset case, and that Δ < 0 forces finiteness.

The product-theoretic motivation from Problem 44 is omitted: this class is closed under Cartesian products, and if the Cartesian product of two sequentially differential posets each with at least two ranks is again sequentially differential, then the factors and the product all have arithmetic-progression r-vectors with the same Δ.

To be fully stand-alone, the question should say explicitly that the objects sought are distributive lattices/posets carrying the sequential differential structure, since the paper alternates between 'r-differential distributive lattice L(r)' and 'finite distributive differential posets.'
The phrase 'Cartesian exponentials of the 2-element and 3-element chains' should be unpacked as finite Cartesian powers of the 2-element chain and of the 3-element chain.
No ambient ring/field, homogeneity, degree, or nilpotency data are relevant here; the missing details are order-theoretic definitions and quantifiers.
refined_question: Let P be a distributive lattice that is also a sequentially differential poset in the sense referenced in [Stan1990, sec. 2], and suppose its associated r-vector (r_0, ..., r_{N-1}) is an arithmetic progression r_i = r_0 + iΔ with Δ < 0, so that P is necessarily finite in the setting of Problem 44. Besides the Cartesian powers of the 2-element chain and of the 3-element chain, do any such finite distributive differential lattices exist, and can all cases with negative common difference Δ be classified completely?
justification: The draft is targeting Problem 44, not a conjecture/theorem statement. Problem 44 explicitly asks whether there are any finite distributive differential posets with arithmetic-progression r-vectors and Δ < 0 other than the Cartesian exponentials of the 2-element and 3-element chains, and whether the Δ < 0 cases can be fully classified. Problem 42 immediately before it supplies the notation L(r) and the uniqueness statement for an r-differential distributive lattice. Because this paper is a notebook of open problems rather than a self-contained development, it does not locally define notions such as 'sequentially differential poset' or 'r-vector'; a stand-alone rewrite therefore has to make those notions explicit while staying within the exact Δ < 0 distributive-lattice scope of Problem 44.
